dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductive family of valid run records indexed by natural dimensions m and n. Its supplied constructor D003 packages matrices A, Q, and R, a floating-point arithmetic model, leading-principal inverses, and all dimensional, triangularity, injectivity, normalization, inverse, and smallness assumptions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem is universally quantified only over values inhabiting this run family, so every assumption stored by D003 is available.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this proposition is the existence of an m by m real matrix G1 satisfying LocalDef004 run G1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the target conclusion: every valid run admits a perturbation matrix G1 with the properties encoded by D004.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor for a run requires 0 < m, 0 < n, n <= m; real m by n matrices A and Q; a real n by n matrix R; injectivity of x mapped to A x; upper triangularity R_ij = 0 whenever j < i; a real epsilonM with 0 < epsilonM < 1; an arithmetic model at epsilonM; exact two-sided inverses for every leading principal submatrix R[0:k,0:k]; the stated smallness inequalities; R_00 equal to the model's computed norm of A's first column; normalization of every A_i0/R_00; and Q_i0 equal to the model division of A_i0 by R_00.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines all hypotheses implicitly carried by the universally quantified run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductive proposition asserting that a proposed m by m real matrix G1 satisfies the first-column backward-error and norm properties introduced by constructor D006.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The existential witness G1 must inhabit this proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef005 n is the type of real n by n matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the dimensions of R, every leading inverse, and the existential perturbation matrix G1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor for LocalDef004 requires R_00 > 0; an error delta with R_00 = ||a||_2(1+delta) and |delta| <= (m/2+1)epsilonM + c2(m)epsilonM^2; Q_i0 = (A_i0+(G1 a)_i)/R_00 for every i; ||G1||_2op <= epsilonM; identification of the one-column residual matrix with e_i = A_i0-Q_i0 R_00; e = -G1 a; equality of the corresponding residual norms; and the bounds ||G1 a||_2 <= ||G1||_2op ||a||_2 <= epsilonM ||a||_2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the complete substantive conclusion required of the existential G1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductive floating-point arithmetic model at unit roundoff epsilonM, constructed by D024 from a normalization predicate, division operation, computed norm, second-order coefficient, and their error axioms.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A run carries such a model, and its operations and error coefficient occur in both the hypotheses and conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The computedNorm projection of an arithmetic model, mapping each finite real vector to a real computed norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the exact stored quantity R_00 and the norm-error equation in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The divide projection of an arithmetic model, a binary real operation modeling computed division.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The run requires Q_i0 = divide(A_i0,R_00).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normalized projection of an arithmetic model, an abstract predicate on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The run assumes normalized(A_i0/R_00) for every row, enabling the model's division-error axiom once the denominator is known nonzero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef011 m n is the type of real m by n matrices, represented as functions Fin m -> Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the types of A, Q, and the one-column residual matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: For natural m and k, this is C(m,k) = alpha(m,k) + 2 beta(m,k), with alpha from D028 and beta from D026.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the coefficient in each leading-principal smallness condition C(m,k+1) epsilonM kappa^2 < 1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given 0 < n, this is the finite index 0 in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects the first row or column entry, especially A_i0, Q_i0, and R_00.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: The identity matrix of the requested square dimension.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The leadingInverse matrices are required to multiply the corresponding leading principal submatrix to the identity on both sides.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: For square matrices R and Rinv, this is ||R||_2op ||Rinv||_2op.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its square appears in the leading-principal smallness hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: For k in Fin n, this restricts R to its leading (k+1) by (k+1) principal submatrix by embedding the smaller indices into Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every such leading block is assumed to have the supplied exact two-sided inverse and to satisfy the smallness condition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary square matrix multiplication over the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the two exact inverse equations for every leading principal block.

dependency_coverage.meaning: The A-matrix projection from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes the input matrix whose first column is analyzed.

dependency_coverage.meaning: The Q-matrix projection from a run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: The R-matrix projection from a run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: The arithmetic-model projection from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies normalized, divide, computedNorm, and the second-order coefficient at the run's epsilonM.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef022
dependency_coverage.meaning: Every run entails 0 < n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It justifies selecting index 0 in the n-dimensional columns and in R.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef023
dependency_coverage.meaning: The epsilonM projection from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the unit-roundoff parameter in all error bounds and smallness assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef024
dependency_coverage.meaning: The arithmetic-model constructor. It requires c2(d) >= 0; for every d-vector x, computedNorm(x) = ||x||_2(1+eta) for some eta with |eta| <= (d/2+1)epsilonM+c2(d)epsilonM^2; computedNorm(x) >= 0; and, whenever y != 0 and normalized(x/y), divide(x,y) = (x/y)(1+eta) for some |eta| <= epsilonM.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These are the only encoded semantic guarantees for the abstract computed norm, division, normalization predicate, and second-order coefficient.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef025
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normSecondOrderCoeff projection c2: Nat -> Real from an arithmetic model.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: c2(m) supplies the second-order term in the computed-norm error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef026
dependency_coverage.meaning: beta(m,k) is 1 when k = 1, and otherwise 2 sqrt(2) m k + 2 sqrt(k), with natural arguments cast to reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It contributes twice its value to C(m,k), the leading-block smallness coefficient.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef027
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proof that the natural numeral 2 is at least two, used to elaborate a real numeral.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is typeclass plumbing for constants and adds no mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef028
dependency_coverage.meaning: alpha(m,k) is m+2 when k = 1, and otherwise (7/2)m k^2 - (3/2)m k + 16k, with natural arguments cast to reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the first summand of C(m,k), the leading-block smallness coefficient.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef029
dependency_coverage.meaning: The m by 1 residual matrix A[:,0] - Q[:,0][R_00], whose entry is A_i0-Q_i0 R_00.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion identifies this residual matrix with its residual vector and then with -G1 A[:,0].

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef030
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an m by 1 matrix, the Euclidean norm of its unique column.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the norm of the first-column residual matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef031
dependency_coverage.meaning: The residual vector e with e_i = A_i0-Q_i0 R_00.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion requires e = -G1 A[:,0] and records the associated norm equalities and inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef032
dependency_coverage.meaning: For k in Fin n, k+1 <= n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It justifies embedding indices of each leading (k+1)-dimensional block into Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef033
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary matrix-vector multiplication: LocalDef033 G x = Gx.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms G1 times A's first column in the perturbed-column equation, residual identity, and norm bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef034
dependency_coverage.meaning: The l2 operator norm of a square real matrix.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines condition-number factors, the bound ||G1||_2op <= epsilonM, and the induced-norm estimate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef035
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite real vector x, sqrt(sum_i x_i^2), its Euclidean norm.

binders: Implicitly universally quantified natural numbers m and n.

A universally quantified run inhabiting LocalDef001 m n. Unpacking the run yields matrices A,Q in R^(m by n), R in R^(n by n), a real epsilonM, an arithmetic model at epsilonM, and one proposed inverse H_s for every leading principal block size s=1,...,n, together with the hypotheses listed below.
hypotheses: The dimensions satisfy 0 < m, 0 < n, and n <= m.
The map R^n -> R^m given by x mapped to Ax is injective.
R is upper triangular in zero-based indexing: R_ij=0 whenever j<i.

The arithmetic model consists of an abstract predicate normalized, an abstract computed division divide, an abstract computed norm computedNorm, and a coefficient c2: N -> R with c2(d) >= 0 for every d.
For every d and x in R^d, there is an eta such that computedNorm(x)=||x||_2(1+eta) and |eta| <= (d/2+1)epsilonM+c2(d)epsilonM^2; also computedNorm(x) >= 0.
For all real x and y, if y != 0 and normalized(x/y), there is an eta with |eta| <= epsilonM and divide(x,y)=(x/y)(1+eta).
For each s=1,...,n, if R_s is the leading s by s principal block of R, the supplied matrix H_s is an exact two-sided inverse: H_s R_s=I_s and R_s H_s=I_s.
Writing a=A[:,0] and r=R_00, the run satisfies r=computedNorm(a) and normalized(a_i/r) for every i.
Writing q=Q[:,0], the run satisfies q_i=divide(a_i,r) for every i.
conclusions: There exists a real m by m matrix G1, depending on the run.
For this G1, r=R_00 is strictly positive.
There exists a real delta such that r=||a||_2(1+delta) and |delta| <= (m/2+1)epsilonM+c2(m)epsilonM^2.
For every row i, q_i=(a_i+(G1 a)_i)/r.
The l2 operator norm satisfies ||G1||_2op <= epsilonM.
If e_i=a_i-q_i r and E is the m by 1 matrix with E_i0=e_i, then the formal residual matrix A[:,0]-Q[:,0][r] equals E.
The residual vector satisfies e=-G1 a.
The unique-column norm of the residual matrix equals ||e||_2, and ||e||_2=||G1 a||_2.
The induced-norm estimates ||G1 a||_2 <= ||G1||_2op ||a||_2 <= epsilonM ||a||_2 hold.
mathematical_definitions: All row and column indices are zero-based finite indices.
For x in R^d, ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum_i x_i^2).
For a finite real matrix M, ||M||_2op denotes its l2 operator norm.
For natural m and s, beta(m,s)=1 if s=1, and beta(m,s)=2 sqrt(2) m s+2 sqrt(s) otherwise, with m and s interpreted as reals.
For natural m and s, alpha(m,s)=m+2 if s=1, and alpha(m,s)=(7/2)m s^2-(3/2)m s+16s otherwise.
For s=1,...,n, R_s is the leading s by s principal submatrix of R and H_s is its supplied inverse.
a=A[:,0], q=Q[:,0], r=R_00, e=a-qr, and G1 a is ordinary matrix-vector multiplication.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of natural dimensions and every valid run containing an injective real m by n matrix A, a real m by n matrix Q, an upper-triangular real n by n matrix R, an abstract floating-point arithmetic model, exact inverses of every leading principal block of R, the specified leading-block smallness assumptions, and the specified computed-norm and computed-division description of the first column, there exists an m by m real perturbation matrix G1 with l2 operator norm at most epsilonM. The first diagonal entry r=R_00 is positive and is the Euclidean norm of A's first column up to a relative error bounded by (m/2+1)epsilonM+c2(m)epsilonM^2. Moreover Q's first column is exactly (a+G1 a)/r, so its residual e=a-qr equals -G1 a, and its Euclidean norm is bounded by ||G1||_2op ||a||_2 and hence by epsilonM ||a||_2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem quantifies over run records rather than arbitrary matrices. For any dimensions or data for which no LocalDef001 run can be constructed, the universal assertion is vacuous.
A run itself forces m>0, n>0, and n<=m, despite the outer theorem quantifying over all natural m and n.
The conclusion concerns only the first column of A and Q and the scalar R_00. It gives no analogous backward-error equation for later columns.
No orthogonality or normalization condition on the full matrix Q is encoded.
No full factorization equation A=QR, approximate or exact, is encoded; only the first-column residual is related to G1.
The matrix G1 and relative-error witness delta are asserted to exist but are not asserted to be unique.

The normalization predicate, computed division, computed norm, and second-order coefficient are abstract and have only the explicitly listed axioms; no particular floating-point format, rounding mode, underflow behavior, or implementation is encoded.
Before the conclusion, the run does not explicitly assume R_00 != 0; it assumes normalized(A_i0/R_00) using total real division. The conclusion strengthens this to R_00>0.
The norm on matrices is specifically the l2 operator norm, not the Frobenius norm.
The leading-principal inverse assumptions are exact two-sided inverse equalities, not approximate inverse statements.
The smallness condition is imposed separately for every block size s=1,...,n and uses C(m,s)epsilonM(||R_s||_2op||H_s||_2op)^2<1.

Several residual-matrix equalities in LocalDef004 explicitly restate definitional identifications between a one-column matrix and its column vector; they are nevertheless fields required by the encoded conclusion.
